item: A crawl or a sitemap index kept to one site reads a link's host after the last @, as the fetcher does (R624)
summary: R624 (Plan's ruling on an independent security read, the follow-up R621's row recorded). BEFORE: src/ingest/crawl.py _registrable_host lower-cased the netloc and cut it at its first ':' before the userinfo was taken out, so https://good.example:x@evil.example/page read as good.example. crawl_source's same_domain_only check queued it and discover_sitemap_urls fetched such a sitemap-index child, both from evil.example, and the evil page was stored as an article of good.example. Robots, the SSRF guard and politeness still applied to evil.example, so no safety check was skipped; the crawl left its stated scope. The same cut read a real same-host userinfo (u:p@good.example) as the host 'u', so the site's own credentialed links and a credentialed start URL were off the site, and every IPv6 literal as '[' and its first group, so [2001:db8::1] and [2001:db8::2] were one site. Only text before the @ holding a ':' was the bug: good.example@evil.example and u:p@evil.example already read as other hosts. NOW: _registrable_host (crawl.py:113) takes the host out of the fetcher's host key (src.ingest._host_netloc, R621): what follows the last @, as urllib.parse reads it, lower-cased, an IPv6 literal without its brackets. The port is still left out (same-site, not same-origin; the sitemap compares with a bare domain that has no scheme to name a default port by); the www. strip and the trailing dot stay as they were. It never raises: a key urllib.parse cannot read again comes back as written and names no site. All four comparisons go through it (crawl.py:172 the start, :224 each link; sitemap.py:202 the base, :223 each child), so neither file reads a netloc by hand any more; sitemap.py gains only a comment. A harvested link or a child sitemap whose netloc holds an @ stays OFF the site even when the host after it is the site (_off_site, crawl.py; the independent read's S1): following it would send the userinfo to the site as a login and write it into the stored article URL, the canonical URL and a saved sitemap address (measured: a robots-declared https://bot:...@good.example/sitemap.xml became Source.sitemap_url), as src/safety/fetcher.py already refuses any userinfo; the base never followed one either (it read the host as 'u'). R630 (Plan's ruling on Steward 3's delta read, folded into this PR): _off_site applied only under same_domain_only, so a crawl with it off still followed and stored such a link, and a sitemap urlset's page address was never checked. A harvested link whose authority holds an @ is now skipped before the scope check, whatever the scope (crawl.py, src.ingest._carries_userinfo), and a urlset page address holding one is never kept, counted in skipped_off_host through failure_url (sitemap.py). Only the start URL and the source domain are read through the key, so a start URL written with a login keeps its host. The sitemap's off-host and error lines write the URL through failure_url (R621). Port 0 joins the default port in the host key (src/ingest/__init__.py _readable_host_key): requests drops ':0' and connects to the default, so 'host:0' was a politeness key of its own (the read's note). A link holding a backslash before an @ that urlparse reads as the site (urllib3 reads the other side) is now on the site and is refused by the fetcher's _refuse_parser_mismatch (R622) before any request, where before it was skipped as off the site; nothing is requested either way. TESTS: tests/test_crawl_scope_userinfo_r624.py, 79, through the real crawl_source and discover_sitemap_urls with a real EthicalFetcher over an in-memory session (every planted evil.example URL routed, so a follow is seen). 29 fail on b3295749d: the colon-userinfo links (:x, :443, an empty password, www., capitals) through both paths, the helper's last-@ and IPv6 reads, two IPv6 hosts kept apart, a credentialed start, and (in the first commit) a same-host userinfo followed, which the fold turned around: it is now pinned as never followed, never sent and never stored, in the crawl and the sitemap. 29 pass there: the controls (capitals, the default port, another port, www., a relative link, IPv6 capitals, a plain host) and the variants that must stay off (no colon before the @, u:p@evil.example, a backslash either side, %40 for the @, a port hiding a %40), never requested on either side. Ten mutants, none survived: the old cut put back; the host key not taken (killed only by the direct u[x@good.example row: through the callers urlparse refuses that URL first); the port kept; the www. strip dropped; the ValueError guard, the 'or ""' and the as-written fallback each removed; and each of the crawl's two and the sitemap's child comparison reading the netloc by hand again. The fold adds 13 tests (the @ rule, port 0, the robots-declared credentialed sitemap, a www. source domain, the as-written fallback exactly) and seven mutants, none survived: the @ rule dropped; the crawl's link check and the sitemap's child check each back to the bare host comparison; the off-host line written raw; port 0 kept; the fallback lower-cased and cut; the sitemap base without the www. strip. The R630 fold adds 8 tests: an open-scope crawl never follows four credentialed link forms, a plain off-site link is still followed there, a credentialed urlset page address is never kept (two forms) and a plain one is; 6 fail on the fold's source (6dd9b14fe), the 2 controls pass. Seven R630 mutants, none survived: either skip dropped; the crawl skip only under same_domain_only; the loc skip not counted, or written raw; either skip widened to every link. NOT CHANGED, the same pattern elsewhere in src/, none deciding a scope or a safety check: link_analyzer/extractor.py:523 compares whole netlocs (equal netlocs are one host, so no other host reads as internal; a same-host link with a userinfo, a port or www. reads as external and is stored as an ArticleLink with its userinfo), and :277/:355/:477 keep the userinfo in the domain label its social/ad/tracking substring checks read; events/feeds.py:101/:885 match the bundled catalogue's own URLs against a dead-host list; law/track.py:800 keys the per-pass deferred-host set by the raw netloc (two spellings of one host are asked twice; never skips another host); database/feed_key.py:38 keeps the userinfo in a feed identity; utils/url_utils.py:157/:267/:290 keep it in canonical URLs (crawl.py:226's dedup then fetches one page twice, once with the credentials, which can reach the stored canonical_url); services/duckduckgo.py:347 keeps it in a result's proposed domain; monitoring/feed_preflight.py:134/:150 show it in a report's host field; catalog/normalize.py:71-73 and privacy/link_sanitizer.py:210 take the last @ (correct) but cut an IPv6 literal at its first ':'; catalog/publicsuffix.py:240, safety/fetcher.py:183 (refuses any userinfo) and src/ingest/__init__.py are correct. Also not changed, in the two files: _harvest_links (crawl.py:134) and the sitemap's urlparse(sm_url) raise a bare ValueError on a malformed href or loc (http://[::1), ending that source's crawl or discovery; and a urlset's own <loc> entries are not host-checked (by the module's design only children are fenced): ruled R626 and R627, one PR after this one; the userinfo labels above are ruled R628. Stated: a backslash child sitemap that urlparse reads as the site now counts against max_sitemaps and is reported as an error (the fetcher's refusal) rather than off-host; nothing is requested either way. Release-notes line: «A crawl kept to one site no longer follows a link that only looks like that site because of text written before an @ in its address, such as https://good.example:x@evil.example/. (R624)» «A crawl or a sitemap no longer follows or saves a page address written with a user name or password, such as https://user:pass@example.org/, on any site. (R630)»
